When you speak into the mic, it transmits the sound waves into the headphones, which then bounce off the earpads and cancel out the original sound waves. This creates a vacuum effect in the ear canal, which blocks out external noises.

The speaker then emits a reverse wave of sound waves that match the frequency of the canceled out sound waves. Since the ear canal is blocked out, the listener hears only the reversed sound waves.
